Mr. Enayetur Rahman ------ For the Respondent No.2 applicant.

full_judgment:
1. This appeal has been preferred under section 28 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 against order No. 9 dated 16.01.2003 passed in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 1/2003 by Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jamalpur refusing to hand over custody of the victim Ishrat Shirin to her engaged lawyers and allowing custody of the victim to her father, who is also informant of G.R. Case No. 989(2)02 arising out of Melandah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 16.07.2002 but on condition that if the victim Ishrat Shirim refuses to go to the custody of her father she will remain in judicial custody. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 16.10.03 so far as it relates to the condition as aforesaid victims father preferred appeal. 

 2. The back ground of the case in which appellant applied for jimma (custody) of his daughter, Ishrat Shirin, briefly is that on 27.10.2001 brother in law of the appellant as informant lodged in F.I.R. with Melandah Police Station against 17 accused persons alleging that Ishrat shahin who is aged about 14 years, student of Class IX of Melandah Government High School was on the way to school on 14.10.2001 at about 9.30 a.m. when unknown persons led by accused Shanin on point of pistol and by wrapping her mouth kidnapped the victim girl and she could not be traced out immediately. Following search here and there the informant also informed the matter to the father of the accused Shahin and went to the house of the matter to the father of the accused then father of the accused admitted that the victim was in his custody and she could be released on condition to marrying her with his son accused Shahin. On receipt of F.I.R. Melandah P.S. Case No. 23 dated 27.10.2001 was started against F.I.R. named accused under section 9(1)/20 Nari -o- Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. In course of investigation Police recovered the victim girl on 27.10.2001 after laps of 14 days from the house of unknown person and on her production before the learned Magistrate the statement of the victim was recorded under section 164 Cr. P.C. on 29.10.01 and she was examined by a Medical Board. Thereafter on the prayer of the father of the victim girl she was released from safe custody and was given in jimma of her father on 29.10.2001. After the victim went to her father's house and had been living there peacefully she made an affidavit denying kabinnama registered on 15.10.2001 and affidavit sworn on 18.10.2001 alleging that they were created by the accused against her will forcibly. Accused Shahin was arrested by police in connection with aforesaid Melandah P.S. Case No. 23 dated 27.10.2001 and was granted bail by the court ' below. Subsequently he was sent to jail again and said accused while in custody on 10.7.2002 at about 6.00 P.M. when the victim girl was going to her uncle's house she was again kidnapped by relatives of accused Shahin out of revenge leading second F.I.R. lodged by the father of the victim whereupon Meladah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 16.7.2002 against 19 accused persons was started. After victim girl was recovered by police she was held in safe custody. 

 3. Police on completion of investigates submitted charge sheets in both the cases. The case was sent to Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Jamalpur where the above two cases were registered as Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case Nos. 47/2002 and 1 of 2003 respectively cognizance was taken and the case was fixed for trial. During of investigation school certificate and connected records of deposit of fee of students including the victim bearing date of birth of the victim was produced by the Head Master of Melandah Government High School before the learned Magistrate cognizance court Jamalpur as directed by the said court. The learned Magistrate by order dated 29.10.2001 allowed the victim girl to go in the custody of the father where she remained until she was remanded to safe custody in jail connection with said Melandah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 16.1.2002. The successive applications for custody of the victim filed by the learned advocate allegedly engaged by the victim proved futile as the same were rejected by the learned Sessions Judge. 

 4. As the case came before the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal. Jamalpur for trial the appellant filed an application praying for 45 releasing his minor daughter in his jimma and while similar petition for custody of the girl to the learned advocates engaged by the victim girl was also filed before the Tribunal. The Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal. Jamalpur after hearing both the petitions together rejected the application filed by learned advocates on behalf the girl and allowed the one filed by the appellant by the impugned order as aforesaid. 

 5. In this appeal the appellant filed an affidavit on 16.3.2003 annexing there to papers namely, the F.I.R. of Melandah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 27.10.2001, statement of the victim under section 164 Cr. P.C. recorded on 29.10.2001, affidavit shown by the victim before the Notary Public, Jamalpur on 13.12.2001 F.I.R. of Melandah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 16.7.2002 on alleged kidnapping of the victim girl for the second time, Order dated 01.02.2003 passed by the Tribunal rejecting the application filed by learned advocate of the victim for custody of the victim girl certificate of the Head Master of Melandah Government Girls High School and school regarding deposit of fees for Registration of the victim girl and others showing the date of birth of the victim girl as on 31.12.1987, subsequent order dated 10.3.2003 passed by the Tribunal allowing joint custody of the victim girl to her advocates, Mr. Anwarul Islam Murad and Mrs. Shamim Ara. as Annexures A, B, C, D, F and (F1) respectively. 

 11. Tania Amir very tenaciously and extensively argued on the question of entitlement of father to the custody of the victim girl in law. The summum bonum of her argument is that if the age of the victim is above 16 years and she is capable of forming her independent opinion the will of such person, when the question before the court is whether she or he should be detained or allowed to go from courts custody must prevail on our query whether the age is at all relevant then her reply is that the age which as relevant is the age in the date on which question is decided. She relied upon a decision of the High Court Division in the case of Anunda Mohan Banerjee v. State reported in 35 DLR-325. In that case the age of victim girl was above 16 years according to school certificate. In the instant case the tribunal has found age of the victim girl as 15 years 16 days on the basis of her date of birth according to school certificate and she is still minor. The facts and circumstances of the case sought to be relied upon are distinguishable. Tania Amir then canvassed that just because the victim girl married the accused she can neither be detained in jail custody nor can she be forced to go to the custody of his father where she refused to go. The learned advocate lastly submitted that matter relating to or arising out of guardianship and custody of child is exclusively triable by family court under section 5 of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. XVIII of 1985) the Tribunal constituted under Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 acted without jurisdiction in allowing custody of the victim to her father. We are unable to accept her contention. Hving regard to the provision of section 25 of the Ain unless otherwise provided by the Ain the provision of the code of Criminal Procedure in the matter of institution of the complaint investigation, trial and disposal there of shall apply and the Tribunal shall be deemed to be sessions court and will exercise all powers of court of sessions on trial of any offence under the Ain or any other offence tribal there under Unfortunately minor girl is victim of offence of abduction and rape of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 under trial of the prosecution in the F.I.R. of Melandah P.S. Case No. 23 dated 27.10.2001 and allegation is that accused Shahin abducted the minor daughter of the informant appellant. The Tribunal is therefore, competent to decide the custody of the victim minor girl. Section 31 of the Ain provides that when safe custody of woman or child is needed she shall have to be kept in the custody of authority, organization of person outside jail. 

 12. In this case according to medical report of the doctors submitted on 12.11.2001 the age of the victim is 17 years. On consideration of the school certificate and school records for deposit of fees of the students of Melandah government Girls High School including the minor the Tribunal found that the date of birth of the victim is 31.12.1987 and present age of the victim is 15 years 16 days and she has not attained the age of majority. Admittedly the victim girl was abducted by the accused on 15.10.2001 and she was recovered by the police on 27.10.2001 the statement of the victim was recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. on 29.10.2001. On the statement of the victim she was allowed to go with her father 

 13. From the impugned judgment it appears that the present appellant and 2(two) learned advocates alleged to have been engaged by the victim filed separate petition praying for custody of the victim girl before the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Tribunal, Jamalpur. It is contended in the application filed by learned advocates on behalf of the minor that doctors found the bony age of the victim as 17 years and she has already attained her majority. Moreover though the victim was given in the custody of her father she refused to go to the custody of her father. This application for custody of the minor girl to the lawyers of her own was opposed by the informant father and also the learned public prosecutor contending inter alia that custody of the victim was already decided in criminal Misc. Cases No. 842/2002, 886/2002 and 994/2002 and upon hearing those criminal Misc Case Nos. 886/2002 and 994/2002 and upon hearing those criminal Misc Case Nos. 886/2002 and 944/2002 at the instance rival contenders were rejected by order dated 27.2.2002 filed by the informant father he was allowed the custody of the minor. These orders were not challenged and set aside by the superior courts and the said orders' remaining unchallenged valid and operative present application filed by the learned advocates for giving her in their joint custody as privately engaged by the victim girl is not maintainable. The medical examination report or horoscope cannot be given preference to the testimony of the father supported by school certificate. According to school certificate and school records of payment of fees for registration issued by the Melandah Govt. Girls High School the present age of the victim is 15 years 16 days and she is still minor and therefore, cannot make her own choice. 

 14. The Tribunal after hearing both sides found inter alia that the jimma of victim girl has already been decided in Misc Case Nos. 842 of 2002, 886 of 2002 and 944 of 2002. The date of birth of the victim girl is 31.12.87 and her present age is 15 years 16 days and she having not attained majority she cannot make her own choice. The father of minor is not only her legal guardian but also best well wisher. Accordingly the Tribunal by order dated 16.1.2003 allowed the application filed by victim's father for giving the victim in his custody and rejected the petition filed by the learned advocates engaged by the victim girl. It appears that after the Tribunal passed aforesaid order dated 16.1.2003 giving the custody of the minor girl to her father the learned advocates privately engaged by the victim instead of challenging the order before the higher courts rather preferred successive petitions before the Tribunal praying for custody on the self same grounds that according the medical certificate issued on 12.11.2001 the age of the victim girl is 17 years and she is major and mature and refused to go to the custody of his father. The Tribunal rejected the subsequent application by order dated 1.2.2003. The Tribunal relied upon the judgment of the appellate Division reported in 7 BLC (AD) -61 that- 

 17. The prosecution case as stated in the F. I.R. is that victim girl Ishrat Shirin who is minor was abducted and raped by accused Shahin. After police recovered the victim and she had been living with her father she was allegedly kidnapped by the relatives of the accused leading to leading of the 2nd F.I.R. It is clearly stated in the 1st F.I. R. of Melandah P.S. Case No. 23 dated 27.11.2001 lodged by the maternal uncle of the victim that the victim is aged about 14 years and she is student of class IX of Melandah Govt. Girls High School and same fact is stated in the 2nd F.I.R. of Melandah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 16.7.2002 lodged by the appellant in connection abdication of the victim and the victim is said to be aged about 14 years 7 months. In the statement of the victim recorded by the learned Magistrate under section 164 Cr. P.C. on 29.10.2001 she herself stated that he was about 14 years age. The victim also made an affidavit before notary public on 13.12.2001 where she stated her age to be about 14 years. From the School certificate annexure E1 issued by the Head Master of Melandah Govt. High School;, duly attested by the Magistrate 1st Class and cognizance court, Jamalpur it is revealed that victim Ishrat Shirin was a student class X of said school and her date of birth is 31.12.1987 from school certificate and memo No. 71/01 dated 27.8.2001 annexure E (2) shows that the said head master of the school deposited Registration fee of this student including the victim girl wherein the name of the victim, her parent and her date of birth is noted as on 31.12.1987 in serial No. 15. 

 18. The Tribunal on consideration of the school certificate and records of registration decided that medical certificate of age issued by the doctor cannot be preferred to the testimony of the age given by the father supported by the school certificate and found the present age of the fact 15 years 16 days as on 16.1.2003 months 22 days. A girl's majority is on attending 18 years of age. This position is admitted by privately engaged advocates of said Ishrat Shirin in the court below. In the application for addition of party filed on behalf of Ishrat Shirin before us nothing is said as to the age of victim. Mr. Enaytur Rahim submitted that the appellant suppressed the fact that applicant Ishrat Shirin's custody is given to her learned lawyers Md. Anawrul Islam (Murad) and Miss. Shamim Ara by subsequent order dated 10.03.2003 as said Ishrat Shirin was not willing to go with her father and that in the memo of appeal filed by the appellant in this court the fact that the operation of the order dated 10.3.2003 was stayed up to 20.3.2003 at the instance of the appellant to enable the appellant to move the High Court Division was suppressed as such the appeal is liable to be dismissed that the High Court Division is competent to pass any order which it thinks fit. We find this allegation of suppression of the fact as to the passing of the subsequent order dated 10.3.2003 as untenable in that in paragraph 9 of the petition filed by the appellant before this court it is clearly stated that the Tribunal by order dated 10.3.2003 allowed the custody of Ishrat Shirin to her aforesaid learned advocates. Mr. Mohammad Ali Jinnah the learned advocate appearing for the appellant filed an affidavit 16.3.2003 annexing the order sheet 10.3.2003 whereby custody of Ishrat Shirin is allowed to her advocate as at annexure-F and order sheet dated 11.3.2003 whereby the operation of the order dated 10.3.2003 has been stayed up to 20.3.2003. The Tribunal in fact passed on order in connection with custody of said Ishrat Shirin on 12.3.2003. In our view the fact that after the impugned order dated 16.1.2003 Tribunal passed another order that is order dated 10.3.2003 makes no' difference for though no hard and fast rule is specifically provided for filing successive application in connection with custody of minor girl in jail such petition may lie in appropriate case subsequent order passed on such application will not invalidate the effect of an order which is otherwise valid in the eye of law automatically and if an appeal is preferred earlier before the High Court Division against one such order out of the series of the orders the appellate court may pass appropriate order for custody notwithstanding the fact that the Tribunal has passed another order in the meantime. On production of the victim girl before us we had the opportunity to see her in our chamber and also to talk to her. On our query she disclosed that according to her medical report she was aged about 17 years as on 12.1.2003 and she is now 19 years of age. In reply to our further query she disclosed the plain truth that the legal costs and fees of the petitioners the learned advocates were borne by accused Shahin. That shows the petition for custody filed by the learned advocates in the name of minor is to set up rival claim for custody against the petition filed by the father. She also disclosed that accused to oppose Shahin's family was well to do. It seems though in jail she spoke under the influence of the accused. If she is 19 she is not required to be in the custody of her advocates. Be that as it may visually the actual age of the girl cannot be ascertained and it also not vry much material. It may be noted that the same victim girl declared her age as 14 years in her statement under section 164 Cr. P.C. It appears from certified copy of the order dated 20.8.2002 passed by the cognizance court Jamalpur produced before us by Mr. Jinnah the learned advocate appearing for the appellant that initially and application was filed by the accused under section 100 Cr.P.C. praying for search warrant which was registered as petition No. 200/2001 and in that when search warrant was issued victim was produced by her father. The victim on dock declared of her own that no one confined her and that she came to court with her father and she would like to go with him. It is true in this case doctor after examining the victim issued certificate and opinion the age of the victim to be 17 years as on 12.1.2001. It is held by the privy council in the case on Md. Saidul Arifeen v. Y.O. Gofrin (AIR-1916 P.B. Council 242) that doctor certificate which is mere opinion and minor declaration before the Magistrate as to age are not proof as to age. 

 19. In the case of Wahid Ali Dewan v. The State and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) -10 it has held that preference cannot be given to other than the testimony of father supported by school certificate. 

 20. In the case of Sree Mongal Chandra Nandi v. Bangladesh reported in 1997 BLD (AD)-33 : 1997 BLT (AD)-l the victim was found to be 15/16 years of age and was ordered to be kept in custody until she attained 18 years as she refused go to her father observing that the observation of the minor girl must be taken with reservation; opinion of the minor is not relevant and it cannot be a factor for not giving the victim to her father. Accordingly the court below was directed to handover the minor to her father. 

 21. In the case of Jharna Rani Shaha v. Khandaker Zahidul Hoque reported in 52 DLR (AD) -66 the appellate Division has held that in the case under Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Ain, 1995 age was not material issue as per detenu she was aged about 18 years, left father's house, embraced Islam and married but as per Horoscope and school certificate the victim was found minor being about 15 years on the date of occurrence and it prima-facie shows that on the alleged occurrence the girl aged about 151/2 years it was it was inhuman to keep the victim in custody but her welfare demands that she should be given to her father and as per law under which the trial is held the girl should remain with her parents as minor cannot make her own choice. 

 22. In the case of Arun Karmokar v. the State reported in 7 BLC(AD) 61 the Appellate Division (per judgment delivered by his lordship Mr. Justice Fazlul Karim) noted with approval the law laid down in the case of Krishnopada Datta v. Secretary Ministry Home Affairs and others 42 DLR -297 where in it was held :- 

 "We are in respectful agreement with the views expressed in Muthu Ibrahims case 11B 37 and 567 and in the case of Sukhendra Chandra Dash, 42 DLR -79 that for the purpose of the custody of the girl age of majority laid down in the Majority Act 1875 read with guardian and words Act 1890 i.e. the age of 18 years is the determining factor to decide, whether the girl is to be given to the custody of the guardian or she is major. It is needless to state that reference to age of 16 years in case of female minor in section 361 of the Penal Code is only for the purpose of commission of the offence of Kidnapping punishable under section 363 of the penal code and not for the purpose of the deciding whether the girl is sui juris." 

 23. Accordingly the Appellate Division held in the case that doctor certificate as to the age of the victim at 17 1/2 years of age and the declaration of the victim made in the statement under section 164 Cr. P.C. of the victim that she was major are no proof of age and that radiologist opinion cannot be preferred to positive evidence of father supported by school certificate. 

 27. In view of the above we find that the condition attached by the Tribunal that if the minor victim refuses to go the custody of father she will remain in judicial custody is prima-facie misconceived and erroneous and it is liable to be set aside. 

 It is directed that the victim will remain in custody of her father till disposal of the criminal case by the Tribunal as well as till she attains the age of 18 years. 

 32. The appeal under consideration got genesised from the order dated 16th of January, 2003 passed by the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal. Jamalpur (hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal"), in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 1 of 2003, whereby the said Tribunal allowed the prayer tabled by the informant/appellant who happens to be the father of the victim of the alleged offence abduction.(hereinafter referred to as the father) for the "jimma" of the victim girl, who has hitherto remained in prison pursuant an earlier Ordered passed by the inquiry Magistrate. The said jimma Order, however, contained a string to the effect that the victim would remain in judicial custody should she decline to make her way to her father's abode. 

 36. On the 7th October, 2001, Shahin. who stands accused in the said abduction case. was apprehended. On 10th July, 2002, during the twilight period, the victim was allegedly kidnapped second time around by Shahin's relatives, but was, subsequently salvaged by the police. whence she was taken to safe custody. The appellant lodged another First Information Report with the police, which culminated in Malandah P.S. Case No. 10 of 16th July, 2002 under Section 5 and 7 of the Act. implicating as many as twelve accused. including Shahin. 

 37. After investigating on both the Information Reports, Police submitted charge sheets in respect to both the occurrences and the Tribunal, having taken cognizance of the offences; the case got recorded as Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 47 of 2002 and Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 1 of 2002, respectively. The victim was and remained at that time, in safe custody pursuant to an Order previously passed by the inquiring Magistrate. 

 42. The learned advocate for the victim's father and the victim suo, being Mr. Mohammad Ali Jinnah and Mr. Enayetur Rahim, respectively, preferred their respective side's argument- I would say, rather tooth and nail, and of course, to their optimum stretch. In addition, Mrs. Sigma Huda and Ms. Tanya Amir, both of whom have veritable treasure of expertise in conspecific cases, made submissions. 

 43. Mr. Zinnah's core points of submission were that the victim, not having attained the age of consent, the learned Tribunal below. misdirected itself by attaching a qualification to the impugned Order, giving the victim option to have the last word on her destined dwelling. To top us this argument, he cited the Appellate Divisions decisions in the case of Arun Karmakar V. State 7 BLC(AD) 61, and argued that the desire of a minor girl about the choice of home, was irrelevant, He further argued that as between two visibly contrapuntal evidence on the age of the victim, the one stemming from the school registry is to be preferred, because of the innate unreliability of the medical evidence on age. Mr. Zinnah went to contend that the learned Tribunal below erred in law in passing subsequent Orders without first setting aside the previous ones and that the first Order was not challenged by the victim. 

 44. Mr. Rahim on the other hand, submitted that since the first Order was a conditional one, it died a natural death when the rider attached thereto foundered and the subsequent Order giving jimma to her advocate reigned. He went on argue that the victim's alleged age as portrayed by her school certificate was as are the cases in our part of the world, far from authentic. He asked us to assess the victim's age ourselves and not to be indifferent to her own aspiration as she is visibly an adult. He continued by arguing that the victim having married Shahin, her only destiny can be the threshold of her husband and that the tug of war is being internally detrimental to the victim's life, future and her health, physical as well as mental. 

 45. Mrs. Sigma Huda and Ms. Tanya Amir argued that the victim's cherished desire. particularly when prima facie she had the appearance of a sui juris, cannot be withered away. They put emphasis on the liberty aspect of the victim. Submitting that power conferred by Section 31 of the Act is a maiden and a new generation one, and this case being the first one to attract this Division's scrutiny on the ambit of said power they asked us to interpret the said Section and define the boundary of the power conferred by the said statutory scheme keeping in mind the cannon of "Purposive Interpretation of Statuses". Both of them contended that the decisions cited by Mr. Zinnah were totally inapplicable to an appeal under Section 28, challenging an Order passed by the Tribunal brought into life by Act VIII of 2000 (the Act). 

 46. Having considered the submissions and perused the records, nourishing in mind the applicable statutory and legal regimes, and pivotally, the nature of the challenge. I arrived at the view that the issues that had to be unfolded to dispose of this appeal were of threefold dimension, namely, (I) whether the instant apparent appeal is maintainable at all and, (II) whether, if the appeal is not maintainable in law this Division case revise the impugned Order under Section 435 and 439 of the Code and if so what Order is to be passed. (III) whether the decisions cited, had any applicability in the instant case. 

 49. Section 28 reads:“ট্রাইবুন্যাল কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত আদেশ, রায় বা আরোপিত দন্ড দ্বারা সংক্ষুব্ধ পক্ষ উক্ত আদেশ, রায় বা দন্ডাদেশ প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে ষাট দিনের মধ্যে, হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে আপীল করিতে পারিবেন। So only an aggrieved party can lodge an appeal. Section 31 reads: “এই আইনের অধীন কোন অপরাধের বিচার চলাকালে যদি ট্রাইব্যুনাল মনে করে যে, কোন নারী বা শিশুকে নিরাপত্তামূলক হেফাজতে রাখা প্রয়োজন, তাহা হইলে ট্রাইবুন্যাল উক্ত নারী বা শিশুকে কারাগারের বাহিরে ও সরকার কর্তৃক এতদুদ্দেশ্যে নির্ধারিত স্থানে সরকারী কর্তৃপক্ষের হেফাজতে বা ট্রাইব্যুনালের বিবেচনায় যথাযথ অন্য কোন ব্যক্তি বা সংস্থার হেফাজতে রাখিবার নির্দেশ দিতে পারিবে।” The word "পক্ষ" in Section 28 in my view, can only mean "a party in the proceeding" which, in my view again, include the victim suo the State as the prosecutor. those who are accused in the indictment, and any woman or a child, who is subjected to sale custodial Order per Section 31. By no stretch of imagination, can the complainant in a public prosecution: he termed as a party in a prosecution which proceeds at the instance of the state. Language in Section 28 is all the more clear in indicating that the phrase "পক্ষ" cannot go beyond those people who are listed above. Again Section 31 contemplates no application from anybody, but confers a discretion upon the Tribunal to act of its own accord and hence the father's application had no nexus with Section 31 or indeed, with any other provision of the Act. The victim in relation to whom the Order had been passed was best placed to prefer an appeal, but she did not. Her father cannot, under the Act be her alter ego. The course that was open to the father was to prefer a habeas corpus application either under Section 491 of the Code or under Article 102 of the Constitution in which case the decisions cited by Mr: Zinnah would, have been pertinent. Without doing that he field this abortive and futile application in the Tribunal which was beyond the Tribunal's jurisdiction to entertain. Hence, I am of the view that the lather not being a persona designate by Section 28, had no locus standi to lodge the apparent appeal and hence there is in the eye of the law , no appeal before us. 

 54. The legislators, however, embarked upon a. so far unexplored, endeavor to fortify the Tribunal with a, hitherto unknown, power the curtail the liberty of "any woman or child" who is not accused of an offence, under the Act and towards that end inducted Section 31, understandably to weed out the predicaments that remained persistent in the past and at the same time to ensure safety of such under aged girls amongst others, in independent dwellings, away from those of their parents, who obstinately refuse to return to parental residence, and who should, in the rational reckoning of the Tribunal, be kept in such independent boarding while the trial of the concerned case remains in progression, without requiring them to be condemned to prison. This newly proliferated provision and power is not only yet to fully emerge out or it's toddler's cot. but has still remained in judicially spinster. 

 56. Section 100 of the Code of Criminal Procedures, frequently picked up by Magistrates to make safe custodial Orders. whether it empowers passage of such Order or not. is a power exclusively retained for Magistrates, subject, however, to judicial scrutiny by such Courts to which, under the Code, and/or the Constitution the Magistrate's Orders are amenable to be examined by way of appeal, revision, or Writ jurisdiction. While the Tribunal had independent and overriding power under Section 31 to send the victim to "safe custody", notwithstanding any Order the enquiry Magistrate previously passed. revising an Order passed by the inquiry Magistrate, who did actually send the victim to the custody, was far beyond the competence of the Tribunal, which does not enjoy revisional or appellate powers granted to the Court of Sessions by the Code. Sending the victim to a custody in exercise of power conferred by Section 31 is one thing, while modifying Magistrates Order, outside the ambit of Section 31 is quite another and it is the second one what the Tribunal has effectively done in the instant case. Although Section 25(1) of the Act says : 

 The natural sequel, then, is that, if the impugned Order by the Tribunal was beyond Section 31 or any other provision of the wombing Act, and was not authorized by any to other enactment, the same must be deemed to have been in the vacuity, a vapid one. In this context I am inclined to be guided by the House of Lord's immortalized decision as pronounced in the horizonic case of Anisminic v. foreign Compensation Commission (1969)2 AC, 147, where the noble Lords of Appeal in the Ordinary. expiated an assiduous distinction between an Order, which falls within the four walls of a statutory scheme and a "purported Order". which does not and hence, cannot be treated to be a Order at all in the eye the empowering statute so as to carry the incidences and the consequences attached to such a statute. In the instant case, for the reasons slated above. I am to say in line with the ratio in Anosmatic case, that what was passed by the learned Tribunal, was not an Order within the remaining and scope of Section 31 of the Act but. were purported Orders, thoroughly vacuous of statutory authority and is therefore, factitious and incapable of being deemed to be an Order within the contemplation of Section 28. The connotation, therefore, is that there could be no question of any appeal under Section 28 against the said stale Order. 

 58. The next question is, whether or not, we can convert the present stillborn appeal in to a revisional case. There are abundance of authorities to preconise that such a move by this Division. ex-debito justitiae remains pleno jure under Section 439 of the Code Erfan Shaikh v. The State ( 9 DLR 424). There are also authorities to dictate that the Court can take suo moto cognizance under Section 439 of the Code (Mahmmad Ali v. The State 37 DLR-261). Plentitude of authorities also support the view that the powers of this Division under Section 439, are wide enough to meet ends of justice. should given circumstances long for the same. 

 59. The fact that the Order purportedly passed by the Tribunal was palpably. patently and indeed, admittedly outside its jurisdiction, being beyond the power conferred by the Demiurge or any other legislation, espoused with the fact that the innocent victim has remained vilipended in a prison captivity with common criminals, in a state of unpalatable misery. in my view, makes the present case highly deserving one for such a conversion, suo motu as per Section 439 of the Code. Considering the ratio of the above cited cases. I find no impediment in this Division's competence, as the Revisional Court, in considering Section 31 and passing consequential Orders. 

 60. I do therefore, being satisfied as per Section 435 that the Order of the Tribunal was not correct legal or proper, hold that pursuit to convert the present case to a revisional one. in view of the nolum legis of the apparent appeal. is well paved, and I am inclined to proceed through the same accordingly. 

 61. At the very inception of assumption of revisional jurisdiction, I must say that in the exercise of said jurisdiction under Section 439 the ideal thing would have been to send the case on remand with direction to the Tribunal to consider Section 31. But the predicament and the ordeal, the victim has been through, would turn further perilous through further efflux of time if the case be sent on remand and hence the same should be disposed of by this Division in entirety. 

 62. It is well settled that an appeal is effectively the continuation of trial and that the appellate forum is fortified with almost all the powers vested on the trial forum. Section 439, confers upon this Division any of the powers conferred on a Court a Appeal by Section 423, amongst other Sections, and Section 423(1)(c) and (d) empowers a Court to alter or reverse "any other" Order (meaning Orders other than those of conviction or acquittal) passed by an inferior Court. I bear in mind that the Order passed or an Order contemplated by Section 31, is not quasi criminal and certainly, also not quasi civil, but a sui generis, a hybrid Order. The Code provisions, are nevertheless applicable to the impugned Order as well as to an Order under Section 31 - in my view, mutatis mutandis - because Section 25 of the Act has made the same applicable. inconsistencies, excepted. Preponderance of authorities show that powers exercisable by this Division in appeal and in revision. with two exceptions (not applicable in the instant case) are similar in all respects (Md. Shamsul Huq v. The State 20 DLR. 540). I do also remain convinced that inherent powers, as preserved by Section 561/A are also ripe for application in this case as an alternative to Section 439, because by passing an extra-jurisdictional Order, the Tribunal, sine dubio. indulged upon an abuse of the process of the Court. Additionally, otherwise to secure the ends of justice, this Divisions competent enough by virtue of it's said inherent power to reverse the non-jurisdictional Order and substitute the same with jurisdictional one as authorised by the parent Act. In this context I bear in mind the decision in the case of Aminul Islam v. Mujibur Rahman 45 DLR (AD) 9, wherein inter relationship between revisional power and inherent powers as preserved by Section 561/A, has been discussed at some length. 

 64. The next and the final question is whether the decisions cited Mr. Zinnah are applicable in the instant case. I am of the view that it would suffice to say that since those decisions, springing from habeas corpus petitions, involving entirely and fundamentally different legal regime and consideration and the issues in those cases being diametrically different those decisions are strangers to the present case. Powers conferred by Section 31 are sui generis power and since none of the cases. cited by Mr. Zinnah. came to this Court by way of appeal under Section 28 or even against any Order or purported Order passed by the Tribunal, created by Act VIII of 2000(the Act), or had any nexus whatsoever with Section 31 of the Act, those decisions have no relevance at all to the instant case. All of those cases involved the questions of the legality of confinement of such women. who were not accused of any offence. In deciding those questions, as a corollary the question of the age of minor girls and the question of the relevance of their desire also propped up because in those cases this Division had to deicide as to in whose custody a non aged girl should be set at liberty to. Although the question of hizanat are for the family Courts under Section 5(e) of XVII Ordinance 1985, to be resolve as per the provisions of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 and the Sharia law regulating "hizanat" as the Appellate Division Ordained in the case of Arun karmakar v. State 7 BLC(AD) 61 this Division ought to and is quite competent to assume all the powers under the Guardians and Wards Act. while considering a habeas corpus petition challenging the internment of a minor girl. 

 65. We are not considering a habeas corpus petition under Section 491 or Article 102 of the Constitution, but are hearing an appeal under Section 28 of the Act (or a converted revisional case per Sections 435 and 439 of the Code). So the principles enunciated in those cases are totally out of place in the case we are concerned with. 

 67. In view of above I do pass an Order as per Section 31 of the Act to vest the victim in the custody of a sanctuary named "Proshanti". situate at 12/B. Agargaon Dhaka, which is managed by Bangladesh National Women Lawyer's Association, of which Advocate Sigma Huda (who volunteered to lake the victim to that asylum), is the Chair and Advocate Sima Jahur is a lawyer. where she will stay either upto the end of the trial of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Cases No. 1 and 47 of 2002 or until her attainment of majority as defined by the Guardians and Wards Act (following proclamation in the case of Arun Karmakar ante), or upto the time when the fog endangering her well being. physical or mental, subsides, whichever is earlier. The case is disposed of accordingly without any Order as to cost. 

 70. During the said session, she did, without vacillation, and without being cryptical and in my view, fearlessly vow, impromptu, that, come what may, she is and would obsequiously remain in nuptial tie with Shahin, even after we reminded her that Shahin may be convicted for abduction even if it is established that she followed him ex-proprio motu, if it is proved that on the dale of occurrence, she was yet to be a sui juris and that he may also be guilty of rape, if she is found to have been under fourteen years of age on the relevant day. irrespective of her consent. With a emotionally charged expression she wished us to accept that a woman marries only once, confirming, that her marriage has been consummated that she would not go back to her father, that her father and uncle are really destroying her future and tranquility and that the so-called affidavit purportedly signed by her, disowning her marriage to Shahin, was in fact produced to her in blank which she signed when assured that she would be allowed to go back to her husband on signing it. She said that like many other cases, her age also was recorded in the School registry with younger depiction. 

 71. I also feel inclined to project the anomalies in the law that often frustrate the very purposes for which a series of law have been enacted to protect minor girls and women. I am totally consentaneous, with my Lord, my learned Senior [Brother that at times we should remain nonchalant towards vealy wishes of under aged girls, who often act irrationally and on whim to their own detriment and that a father is a child's best well wisher. Legislations to curb repression against women have gone some way to attain this goal, but not as much as are warranted and are in many instances distorted by anomalies. For example, even as of today, the husband of a minor who, may land on prison under the Act as well as under the provisions of Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, as amended by Ordinance VIII of 1961, for marrying a minor, may nevertheless bring an action for Restoration of Conjugal Rights, under Section 5(b) of Ordinance XVIII of 1985. While a restitution Order would be without teeth in respect to an unwilling wile, and such an Order has been specifically made in executable by the Code of Civil Procedure, if the wife be willing, such an Order may entail far reaching and sinister consequences and, may subject the parents themselves to come under the Ordeal attached to Section 99 and 100 of the Code or may even render them to be charged for abduction. because, all the laws that propose to protect under aged girls, are penal in nature, none of which affect the validity of the marriage, if they be otherwise valid. Hence further legislative intervention is required to attain repletion of satisfaction by making marriage to an under eighteen girl, not only punishable, but also void ab-initio. If a marriage is not a sacrament, but a contract and, is dependant on the consensuality of the parties, there exists no reason why provision similar to that in Section 11 of the Contact Act, should also not be made applicable to marriage contracts and Section 2 of the Majority Act 1875 should not be amended. In the instant case, however. I am of the view that, as of today, the victim is. prima facie, no younger than eighteen and is mature enough to perceive her well-being and hence, had this been a case under Section 491 of the Code, I would still have felt inclined to release her to go to a place of her choice. I do however reiterate that her age must be left to be determined during the trial without and reference to what we prima facie, found. 

 72. It is her said expressed agony, for which I felt all the more inclined to hold that she is a suitable person for safe custody under Section 31 of the Act, otherwise, for the reasons stated above, the question of her age. relevancy of her desire and question of the validity and the consequences of the claimed marriage reflects nothing more than interests of academic nature in the instant case. 

 74. This appeal has been preferred under section 28 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain. 2000(hereinafter referred to as the Act) against the order No. 9 dated 16.1.2003 passed by Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal Jamalpur (hereinafter referred to as the tribunal) in Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. I of 2003 allowing the prayer of the father of the victim girl for giving her in his custody with a condition that if the victim girl refuses to go to the custody of her father she will remain in judicial custody. Victim's father Md. Nannu Miah, being aggrieved by this condition attached to the order allowing his prayer for the custody of his daughter, has preferred this appeal. 

 75. The short facts which are necessary for the disposal of this appeal are that Victim Ishrat Shirin was a student of class IX of a local school. On 14.10.2001 at 9.30 A.M. while she was going to her school she was allegedly kidnapped by accused Shahin and his other accomplices. On 27.10.2001 one maternal uncle of Ishrat Shirin lodged an F.I.R. with Melandah P.S. against 17 accused persons alleging that Ishrat Shirin aged about 14 years was kidnapped by accused Shahin and other F.I.R. named accused persons from the way to her school. On the basis of that F.I.R. Melandah P.S. case No. 23 dated 27.10.2001 under section 9(1)/20 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 was started. During investigation the police recovered the victim girl on 27.10.2001 and on 29.10.2001 she was produced before the Magistrate where she made a statement under section 22 of the Act. stating that she was kidnapped by the accused Shah in and others and was also raped by accused Shahin against her will. On her such statements the learned magistrate released the victim Ishrat Shirin in the jimina of her father. In the meantime main accused Shahin was arrested by the police and thereafter on 10.7.2002 Ishrat Shirin was again kidnapped by the accused persons. On 16.7.2002 Nannu Miah the lather of the victim Ishrat Shirin lodged the 2nd F.I.R. against accused Shahin and his other relations and friends and on the basis of this 2nd F.I.R. Melandah P.S. Case No. 10 dated 16.7.2002 was started. The police recovered the Victim girl again and this time the victim was sent to the judicial custody inside the jail by the learned Magistrate and since then i.e. since 16.7.2002 the victim Ishrat Shirin is in jail custody. 

 76. The police completed investigation of both the above mentioned cases and submitted charge sheet in both the case against the accused persons. Both the cases were ultimately sent to the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal. Jamalpur for trial and those were numbered as Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 47 of 2002 and Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 1 of 2003 which was subsequent renumbered as Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 6 of 2003. Before the Tribunal this appellant Mr. Nannu Miah filed an application praying for releasing his minor daughter in his "jimina". Another similar. petition was also filed on behalf of the victim herself by her engaged lawyers praying for custody of the girl to her engaged lawyers. The Tribunal, after hearing both the parties, rejected the prayer of the engaged lawyers of the victim and allowed that of the father of the victim with the condition as has already been stated above. In this appeal the father of the victim has challenged this very condition attached to the impugned order allowing the custody of the victim girl to her father. 

 77. His lordship Mr. Justice Khademul Islam Chowdhury by his judgment has allowed this appeal setting aside this very condition attached to the impugned order and also directing the Deputy Commissioner. Jamalpur to release the victim girl Ishrat Shirin forthwith and hand over her to her father on the same bond and surety fixed by the tribunal. Mr. Justice Khademul Islam Chowdhury has held the view that since the victim Ishrat Shirin prima facie appears to be a minor her welfare would be best served if she is given in the custody of her father. On the other hand Mr. Justice A.H.M. Shamsuddin Chowdhury has held the view that the victim's father cannot maintain this appeal and he is not also entitled to gel custody of her daughter under section 31 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain.2000. Mr. Justice A.H.M. Shamsuddin Chowdhury therefore. in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has passed an order to vest the victim in the custody of a sanctuary named "Proshanti" situated at 12/B, Agargaon, Dhaka with a direction that the victim will stay there either upto the end of the trial of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Cases No. 1 of 2003 and 47 of 2002 or until her attainment of majority or upto the time when the fog endangering her well being, physical or mental, subsides. whichever is earlier. 

 79. I have heard the learned advocates for both the sides at length. Mr. Mohammad Ali Zinnah the learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that in this case the papers which have come before the court prima facie show that the victim is a minor till date. The learned advocate has pointed out that as per direction of the Tribunal the concerned school authority sent a certificate as regards the date of the victim girl and this school certificate shows that the date of birth of the victim girl is 31.12.1987 i.e. today her age is 15 years 7 months 12 days. The learned advocate has been candid to point out also that the victim Ishrat Shirin was examined by the doctor for the purpose of ascertaining her age and as per that doctor's report dated 12.11.2001 her age was about 17 years. The learned advocate Mr. Mohammad Ali Zinnah has cited some decisions in support of his contention that school certificates as to the age supported by the testimony of the father will get preference to the report of the doctor. 

 81. However, it appears that in their respective judgments their lordships both Mr. Justice Khademul Islam Chowdhury and Mr. Justice A.H.M. Shamuddin Chowdhury have concurred on the point that the age of the victim Ishrat Shirin must be left to be determined by the Tribunal on trial. I also, in agreement with the above view, am of the opinion that the actual age of the victim girl Ishrat Shirin will be determined by the Tribunal on trial. However. for the present purpose the school certificate and the statement of the own father of the victim prima facie show that the victim is still a minor- her age being much less than 18 years. Of course according to the doctors report the victim Ishrat Shirin is a major now. But in many cases the appellate Division has held that the doctor's certificate as to age being a mere opinion is no proof of age and it cannot be preferred to testimony of the father supported by the school certificate. Some of these decisions of the Appellate Division have been quoted in the judgment written by Mr. Justice Khademul Islam Chowdhury. In the present case not only the statement of the father and the school certificate, but also the own statement of the victim herself show that the present age of the victim is much less than 18. In the statement of victim recorded by the magistrate on 29.10.2001 under section 22 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain.2000 and also in the affidavit sworn by the victim on 13.12.2001 the victim slated her age as 14 years. All these papers prima facie show that the victim Ishrat Shirin is still a minor-her present age is much less than 18 years. 

 82. It is not denied that the father being the legal guardian and also that the best well wisher of his minor child is entitled to get the custody of his minor child. But in the present case it appears that the 'wish' of the victim girl has played the main role in determining her custody by the tribunal and also by Mr. justice A.H.M. Shamsuddin Chowdhury. It appears that Mr. justice A.H.M. Shamsuddin Chowdhury on observing the victim girl Ishrat Shirin personally in their Chamber and upon questioning her formed an impression that the girl prima facie appeared to be not less than 18 years and that she was not willing at all to go her lather's abode. Had it been the actual state of affairs I would have found no reason to differ with the decision given by Mr. Justice A.H.M. Shamsuddin Chowdhury. But on going through the record and some material papers submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Mohammad Ali Zinnah I find the state of affairs otherwise. It appears that after recovery of the victim first time on 27.10.2002 this victim Ishrat Shirin herself made statement before the Magistrate under section 22 of of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 slating that she was kidnapped by the accused persons and was raped. On her such statements the learned magistrate gave her to the custody of her father without any objection from her. Thereafter also, on 13.12.2001 the victim Ishrat Shirin sworn an affidavit affirming her statement that she was kidnapped forcibly by the accused persons. On 21.1.2002 the victim Ishrat Shirin was again produced before the Magistrate on a prayer of the accused Shahin made under section 100 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and this time also the victim clearly stated that she was willing to remain in the custody of her. father. Thereafter, on 10.7.2002 the victim was again allegedly kidnapped by the accused persons and was recovered on 16.7.2002 and this time, for the first, she refused to go to her father's custody. But it appears that again on 18.6.2003 this victim Ishrat Shirin herself filed a written petition to the jail authority stating that she was willing to go to the custody of her father. The photo copy of this petition written by the victim herself with her own hand was produced by the learned advocate for the appellant before this court on 2.7.2003. But the learned advocate Mr. Einayetur Rahim expressed his suspicion that this alleged petition of the victim might not be genuine. Considering this suspicion of the learned advocate Mr. Enayetur Rahim I directed of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal. Jamalpur to examine victim Ishrat Shirin personally to ascertain whether she was actually willing to go to her father's custody and to report. Accordingly the said Tribunal has sent a report to this court staling that before him the victim Ishrat Shirin stated that though she filed the petition for going to the custody of her father but now she was not willing to go to the custody of her father. However, this report of the Tribunal proves that victim Ishrat Shirin herself filed the above stated petition dated 18.7.2003 to the jail authority for releasing her in the custody of her father. Photo copy of the said petition of the victim Ishrat Shirin attested by the Special public Prosecutor. Jamalpur has been filed before me from the side of the appellant and it is in the record. This petition appears to be of own hand writings of the victim Mst. Ishrat Shirin. The last petition of this petition reads thus :- 

 83. So, I endorse the decision of Mr. Justice Khademul Islam Chowdhury that the victim Ishrat Shirin will remain in the custody of her father till disposal of the above stated cases or till she attains the age of 18 years. The father of the victim however, will not take any initiative to make the victim divorce the accused Shahin if their is at all any valid marriage between them and to give her in marriage with any other person till disposal of the instant cases by the tribunal. 

 84. Before conclusion 2 other questions raised by Mr. Cnayetur Rahim should be answered Both the questions relate to the maintainability of this appeal. The learned advocate has first argued that the father of the victim is not a party of this case and as such this appeal filed under section 28 of the of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain. 2000 is not maintainable at all. The learned advocate has drawn my attention to the judgment written by Mr. Justice A.H.M. Shamsuddin Chowdhury wherein it has been held that "by no stretch of imagination can the complainant in a public prosecution be termed as a party in a prosecution which proceeds at the instance of the State" But I am unable to accept this view. Section 28 of the of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain.2000 reads thus :- 

 In In the present case the appellant is not only the complainant rather the impugned order also was passed on his prayer seeking custody of his daughter and this order has aggrieved this appellant only. It is well settled that information can prefer an revision under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against a judgment of acquittal where the state does not prefer any appeal. The conferment of this very power on the informant has recognized the informant / complainant as an aggrieved party no doubt. So, my view is that by no stretch or imagination can the complainants or informants he excluded from the category of " সংক্ষুব্ধ " or "aggrieved party" as stated in section 28 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000. 

 85. The learned advocate Mr. Enayetur Rahim has next argued that the impugned order is not passed pursuant to section 31 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and as such it is not an order as contemplated by section 28 of the Act. The contention of the learned advocate is that section 31 does not contemplates father's custody, but custody of any other person, or organization etc. and hence the impugned order giving the victim in the custody in her father is not an order of 'safe custody' as per section 31 of the Act. I do not disagree with the learned advocate on this point that the impugned order has not been passed pursuant to section 31 of the Act. But this order is very much an order as contemplated by section 28 of the Act inasmuch as I find that this order has been passed by the tribunal in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to revise an improper order passed by the enquiry magistrate. Section 25(1) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain.2000 has given this power to the tribunal. According to this section in trying a case under this Act the tribunal shall be deemed to be a Sessions Judge and shall have all the powers of a Sessions Judge and the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure so far these are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act will be applicable in enquiry trial etc. of the cases under this Act. from section 31 of the Act it is clear that this special law has prohibited the safe custody inside jail. So, when it was brought to the notice of the tribunal that the victim girl had been sent to the jail custody by the order of the learned magistrate the tribunal has only revised this order by giving back the victim girl to the custody of her father who is her legal guardian and this the tribunal has done in exercise of his revisional power under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which he was authorized to exercise by section 25(1) of the Act. So this impugned order is very much an order in accordance with law inclusive of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain.2000 and as such it is appealable under section 28 of the Act. It should be clarified here again that the impugned order is not at all a 'safe custody' order as contemplated by section 31 of the Act. 

 The Deputy Commissioner. Jamalpur is directed to release the victim girl Mst. Ishrat Shirin. daughter of Md. Nannu Miah forthwith and hand over her to her father on the same bond and sureties fixed by the Tribunal. The victim will remain in the custody of her father till disposal of the instant criminal cases or till she attains the age of 18 years.
